introduction: On this Sunday, the Law of Moses describes how a person with leprosy had to live apart, outside the camp, crying, Unclean. In the Gospel, a leper kneels before Jesus and says, If you want to, you can make me clean; moved with compassion, Jesus touches him and heals him. Paul tells us to do everything for the glory of God. Let us bring to Jesus whatever makes us feel unclean or alone.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Jesus is moved with compassion for all who suffer. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may reach out and touch those whom others keep at a distance. Let us pray to the Lord.
For people living with leprosy and other diseases that bring stigma: that they may find care, healing and respect. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who feel unclean because of their sins: that they may hear Jesus say, I want to; be made clean. Let us pray to the Lord.
For doctors, nurses and all who care for the sick: that they may serve with the compassion of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that whatever we do, we may do it all for the glory of God. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, your Son was moved with compassion and touched the leper to heal him. Touch us too, make us clean, and send us to reach out to all who are excluded. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: If you want to
reflection.body:
The first reading describes the hard life of a person with leprosy in ancient Israel. The rules were meant to protect the community from disease, but the cost for the sick person was terrible: "He shall dwell alone. His dwelling shall be outside of the camp." Such a person lost not only health, but family, community and worship.

In the Gospel, a leper does something forbidden: he comes right up to Jesus. Kneeling, he says, "If you want to, you can make me clean." He does not doubt that Jesus can heal him. His only question is whether Jesus wants to.

Mark tells us Jesus' response: "Being moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand, and touched him." Jesus touches the man no one would touch. By the Law, touching a leper made a person unclean. But with Jesus the opposite happens: his holiness and health flow into the sick man. And Jesus answers his question: "I want to. Be made clean."

The Church has long seen in leprosy an image of sin, which isolates us from God and from others. Many of us carry something we think makes us untouchable: a sin, a shame, a wound. The leper teaches us to bring it to Jesus with confidence. He wants to make us clean, especially in the Sacrament of Reconciliation.

The healed man cannot keep quiet: he "began to proclaim it much." The psalm expresses the same joy: "Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven, whose sin is covered."

Paul gives us a simple rule for all of life: "whatever you do, do all to the glory of God." And he adds, "Be imitators of me, even as I also am of Christ."

This week, bring to Jesus whatever makes you feel unclean, and ask him to heal you. And reach out to someone who is kept at a distance, through a visit, a call or a kind word.
